verdict_line: A hero product priced like a venture deal. Fundable at roughly $1.1-1.25M today; the granted patent and lower ad dependence are worth the gap to Maya's number.

fixes.title: Get the utility patent granted before the next raise
fixes.why: Lena and Dana both tied value to IP; 'pending' capped the valuation.
fixes.how: Pay for prioritised examination where available and lead with the design patent already filed.

fixes.title: Cut ad dependence below 15% of revenue
fixes.why: Dana went out because half the sales are rented.
fixes.how: Push repeat (31% today) with bundle packs and a subscribe-and-save offer; show organic share by month.

fixes.title: Price the ask off profit, not hope
fixes.why: Victor's 6x-sales jab framed the whole negotiation.
fixes.how: Show contribution per unit, retail purchase orders and next-year profit; ask at a multiple you can defend.

fixes.title: Open with the Coke-on-the-desk story
fixes.why: It won Rosa outright and is the best proof of retail pull.
fixes.how: Make it the hook slide, then do the flip test live.

fixes.title: Bring retail proof, not just Amazon proof
fixes.why: Every interested shark was buying a retail future.
fixes.how: Bring sell-through from the 40 gas stations and at least one signed regional PO.

objections.q: Six times sales for a plastic lid. Why?
objections.weak: It's a habit, and retail hasn't started.
objections.strong: 86% gross margin, 31% repeat, and a [regional chain] PO for [N] stores. On next year's [profit target] this is [multiple]x profit.

objections.q: What happens if you turn off Amazon ads?
objections.weak: Sales would probably drop by half.
objections.strong: Organic is now [x]% of sales, repeat customers are 31%, and the 40 gas stations sell [N] units a week without a single ad.

objections.weak: Utility patent pending, plus a design patent.
objections.strong: Design patent filed, utility patent [status], and we have [N] months of tooling lead over a copier.

objections.q: What is your profit over twelve months?
objections.strong: $38k after a $60k salary and reinvesting in inventory; at retail scale contribution per unit stays near $6.50.

note: Text in [brackets] is a fact only the founder can supply. Fill it in before you pitch.
pitch_v2: Eight times a gas station manager in Ohio told me no. On the ninth visit I spilled a Coke on his desk, then did it again with SnapSip on the can. He took 40 stores. SnapSip is a magnetic lid that turns any can into a leak-proof travel cup. It costs $2.10 and sells for $14.99. In 14 months: $410k in sales, 4.6 stars on 3,900 reviews, 31% buy again. I'm raising $250,000 to fund retail inventory and finish the patent.
metrics_to_bring: Organic vs paid sales by month
Gas-station sell-through per store per week
dd_checklist: Amazon account health and returns rate

next_steps.action: Rewrite the hook around the gas station story and rehearse the flip test.
Launch subscribe-and-save bundles and cut ads to under 15% of revenue.
Go back to investors with a granted patent and one regional retail PO.
